correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the run law, the random-prefix maximum argument, all normalizations, and the transfer to sweeps. On a ring of L >= 3 with a nonempty initial plus set, different minus runs use disjoint site clocks and cannot merge. Given length k, a run has k-1 independent rate-2 waits followed by one independent rate-1 wait, including the k=1 case. Mixing over geometric(p) lengths gives H = E + BW in law with independent E ~ Exp(1), B ~ Bernoulli(1-p), W ~ Exp(2p), so its Laplace transform is p(s+2)/[(s+1)(s+2p)]. The survival function is [p exp(-t)-(1-p) exp(-2pt)]/(2p-1) for p != 1/2 and exp(-t)(1+t/2) at equality. To avoid conditioning marks on the renewal count, embed successive complete runs in an infinite iid marked prefix. Their count divided by L tends in probability to p(1-p), or to 1/4 in the triangular case by bounded second moments of the geometric cycles. Sandwich the maximum pathwise between fixed-prefix maxima of (p(1-p) +/- epsilon)L marks on the count event, then send epsilon to zero. Runs meeting the cut and omitted from the prefix are bounded by the two geometric-tailed boundary fragments; they contribute o(1) at any threshold tending to infinity. The all-plus configuration has time zero, and conditioning away the all-minus event, of probability (1-p)^L, does not affect the limits. For p<1/2 the center is [log L+log(p(1-p)^2/(1-2p))]/(2p), with multiplier 2p; for p>1/2 it is log L+log(p^2(1-p)/(2p-1)), with multiplier 1. At p=1/2 the center is log L+log log L-log 8. In the window p_L=1/2+a/log L, exp[-(2p_L-1)t] tends to exp(-2a) at the stated thresholds, and the leading survival factor is exp(-t)(log L)w(a)/2, where w(a)=(1-exp(-2a))/(2a), w(0)=1. Adding log w(a) to the critical center gives Lp_L(1-p_L)R_{p_L}(t) -> exp(-x); the fixed-density centers give the same intensity at their scaled thresholds. The iid maximum formula then gives exp(-exp(-x)). For de-Poissonization, the first L prefix marks and the boundary lifetime have a uniform positive exponential-moment bound for each fixed p or near p=1/2 (choose the moment parameter also below the geometric-fragment bound). Their union bound gives conditional E[T_L]=O(log L). Independent rate-L interattempt gaps have conditional time-error variance J_L/L^2, with E[J_L]=L E[T_L] under the same conditioning, so the sweep error is o_P(1). The argument is analytic; the uploaded checker was not executed.
residual_risks: The window statement is pointwise for each fixed finite a; no uniformity over growing a or quantitative convergence rate was established.
An unconditional finite-L mean would be infinite because of the all-minus atom; the sweep error estimate is conditional on nonempty initial plus set.

evidence: Ertul's theorems are interval mixing/cutoff results, including a Gaussian-window result under its stated assumptions, rather than order-one absorption profiles conditional on an iid nonempty seed set on a periodic ring.
Shcherbakov identifies the cooperative filling class; the growth theorem inspected concerns multiple occupancy and localization rather than the completion time for saturated one-site filling.
Evans was accessible only at abstract level; broad coverage of adsorption is not evidence for or against an exact finite-ring completion law.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A mixing theorem for the interval is not a Bernoulli-initial ring absorption theorem, and the inspected growth/localization theorem has a different state space and observable. Standard iid extreme-value theory gives the limiting form after the effective tail and count have been derived; it does not supply those model-specific inputs.

evidence: Cao et al. provide the rate-2/rate-1 stages in random-sequential form (success probabilities 2/L and 1/L) for a single fixed run in (C3), and (C4) gives the sweep mean for an arbitrary deterministic length vector. Equation (21) compares the logarithmic mean for fixed short runs with the linear mean for a fixed long run.

The common decay factor (1-1/L)^k noted in §IV.B is a fixed-L, fixed-preparation tail statement. It does not capture the competing 2p exponential rate or a resonance when the run lengths are randomized while L increases.
Ottino-Löffler et al. obtain a Gaussian one-seed cycle limit with infected-source/neighbor updates; Ertul treats interval mixing rather than the iid ring statistic.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the identical generator and the fixed-length lifetime mechanism to Cao et al. A deterministic-vector mean recursion is not a distributional implication, and passing from the deterministic-run stage laws to the claimed profile requires mixing the geometric length, controlling the renewal prefix and the cut, and evaluating the competing tails at the L-dependent normalization. The inspected prior results do not entail the stated law by a direct specialization.

evidence: In cooperative monomer filling use plus = occupied and rates (0,1,1) according to the number of occupied neighbors. This preserves the rate of the final isolated vacancy; an additive edge infection with rates (0,1,2) does not.
In FA-1f notation use plus = vacancy and set the dynamical refresh parameter q=1; the facilitator constraint is then the same local rule. The p in the reviewed theorem is instead an initial density.
Cao et al. §IV.B explicitly define the identical random-sequential ring rule. Ottino-Löffler et al. §II use a different update and a single seed.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Checked exact alternative descriptions as well as a superficially similar cycle infection. Equivalent generators do not transfer a theorem unless the observable, domain and initialization are covered; the inspected FA-1f and adsorption results did not give the Bernoulli ring profile. The edge-based rule changes the last-site waiting time and hence cannot identify its rate collision with this one.

checked_sources: Frozen RESULT.md, equations (1)–(4); Cao et al. §IV.B Eq. (21) for the deterministic preparation contrast.
value.rationale: The natural quantity is the time for the last minus domain to disappear, not the time for a typical site to flip. Its effective decay rate changes from 2p to 1 as the seed density crosses one half. Equal rates change the polynomial multiplier in the tail, leading to a log log L delay, and the order-one crossover constant describes which finite-size normalization applies near that density. This supplies an exact collective passage-time benchmark for a standard kinetic constraint and distinguishes iid preparation from the known deterministic patterns. The scientific contribution is this model-specific classification and window, not the general Gumbel method.
residual_risks: No claim for correlated seeds, nonmonotone dynamics, higher dimensions, or fast finite-size convergence.
